name: Autoimmune Psychosis

criteria.description: New onset psychotic symptoms including hallucinations, delusions, or disorganized thinking
Presence of neuronal surface autoantibodies in serum or cerebrospinal fluid
Exclusion of primary psychiatric disorders and infectious or metabolic causes
Presence of seizures, movement disorders, or cognitive dysfunction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: New onset psychosis plus detection of neuronal autoantibodies and exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is supported by response to immunotherapy and presence of additional neurological signs.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Psychosis with acute or subacute onset

laboratory: Presence of neuronal surface autoantibodies (e.g., anti-NMDA receptor antibodies) in CSF or serum
Elevated inflammatory markers (e.g., ESR, CRP) in some cases
imaging: MRI brain may show T2/FLAIR hyperintensities in limbic regions
FDG-PET may show hypermetabolism in affected brain areas
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; possible HLA associations under investigation
other: Electroencephalogram (EEG) abnormalities including diffuse slowing or epileptiform discharges

distinguishingFeatures: Chronic course without inflammatory CSF findings
Different CSF profile with pathogens detected

differentialDiagnoses.diseaseId: primary mood disorder with psychotic features

redFlags: Rapid onset of psychosis with neurological symptoms
Presence of seizures or movement disorders
Poor response to standard antipsychotic treatment
references: Dalmau J, Graus F. Antibody-Mediated Encephalitis. N Engl J Med. 2018;378(9):840-851.
Pollak TA, et al. Autoimmune psychosis: an international consensus on an approach to the diagnosis and management of psychosis of suspected autoimmune origin. Lancet Psychiatry. 2020;7(1):93-108.
Kayser MS, Dalmau J. Anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis in psychiatry. Curr Psychiatry Rev. 2016;12(3):189-193.
